statement: A September 2026 primary repository claims a resolution of the target; the dated September 7 ranking alone cannot certify that C0041 remains open on October 10.
assumptions: Public search excerpt accurately identifies the repository statement; full proof verification remains pending
proof_or_counterexample: Targeted public search returned the exact target with dimension d>=2, iid uniform ellipticity and positive directional velocity. This is a source lead, not an accepted mathematical result.
remaining_gap: Read actual theorem and supporting argument; check trusted axioms rather than trusting a formalization label.

statement: There are independent attempts with a geometric success count and almost-sure finite individual costs whose total elapsed cost is almost surely finite but has infinite expectation.
assumptions: L_i iid and independent of B_i, with P(L_i=2^k)=2^(-k-1), k>=0
N=first i with B_i=1; C=1+sum_{i<N} L_i
proof_or_counterexample: P(N>n)=(1-q)^n; N and every L_i are finite almost surely. E L_i=sum_k 1/2=infinity. The positive-probability event N>1 already gives an infinite contribution to E C. Truncation at 2^K has E C^(K)=1+((1-q)/q)(K/2+1).
remaining_gap: Independent check pending. This is an abstract negative control, not a d>=2 uniformly elliptic iid RWRE counterexample.

statement: For nested survival events S_i in an increasing filtration F_i, S_1=Omega, E[1_{S_{i+1}}|F_i]<=r 1_{S_i} with 0<=r<1, and nonnegative costs satisfying E[1_{S_i} A_i|F_i]<=a 1_{S_i} with a finite, E[sum_i 1_{S_i} A_i]<=a/(1-r).
assumptions: All random variables and events are measurable; the named filtration is increasing
S_i in F_i and S_{i+1} subset S_i
The two conditional bounds hold almost surely for every i
proof_or_counterexample: Taking expectations of the survival inequality gives P(S_i)<=r^(i-1). Taking expectations of the cost inequality gives E[1_{S_i} A_i]<=a P(S_i). Tonelli and the geometric series give the bound. No independence is assumed.
remaining_gap: Independent check pending; obtaining this cost bound for actual RWRE attempts is unproved and can be stronger than the required annealed first moment.

statement: Fixed-center inward-pattern rarity does not bound an unrestricted environment-measurable selected center.
assumptions: d>=2, kappa=1/(4d); iid rows favor +e_1 or -e_1 with probability 1/2 each
Every direction has probability kappa and the favored direction has an additional 1/2
delta=1/2; r>=1; disjoint candidate boxes have centers j(2r+1)e_1
proof_or_counterexample: Each box event has probability 4^(-r(2r+1)^(d-1))>0 and disjoint-box events are independent. The first matching index is finite almost surely. The selected center matches with probability 1; no deterministic location bound exists.
remaining_gap: No target RWRE counterexample is claimed. This does not meet or refute L3's bounded-center/start conditions.

statement: A summable slow-delay classification error plus logarithmic-size rare-pattern certificates within a polynomial search volume yields an integrable integer-valued duration under a positive-probability conditioning event.
assumptions: d>=2; P_env(A(x,r))<=exp(-a r^d) for all centers and integer r>=1, a>0
Q=P(.|E), P(E)=q>0, c>0, r(t)=floor(c log(t+2))>=1 eventually
Q(T>t)<=epsilon_t+Q(union_{|x|_infinity<=t} A(x,r(t))) eventually; epsilon_t>=0 and sum epsilon_t<infinity
proof_or_counterexample: Bound the conditioned union by q^(-1)(2t+1)^d exp(-a r(t)^d). For d>=2 this is eventually at most (t+2)^(-3). Sum the duration tail.
remaining_gap: The classification inequality is an unproved sufficient input for actual regeneration. It is not supplied by the finite-box lemmas.

statement: For a pre-exit path confined to M states, a uniform conditional probability h of no revisit at each visit yields P(T>t,confined)<=M(1-h)^(floor(t/M)-1) for integers t>=M.
assumptions: T is a stopping time; B is a deterministic set of M>=1 states
At every kth visit to every x in B before T, conditioned on the visit sigma-field, probability of no further visit before T is >=h, 0<h<1
Time and visit counts are discrete
proof_or_counterexample: Tower iteration gives P(K_x>=m)<=(1-h)^(m-1). On confinement and T>t, one of M sites has at least floor(t/M) visits; take a union bound.
remaining_gap: For RWRE one must prove the uniform visit hazard, confinement and width-tail bounds under the correct law. No full-paper or formal check is claimed.
